summary: A woman hears that her husband died overseas, where he was with her co-wife. She must wait to see if the co-wife is expecting a baby, because then she would be free of yibum. The mishnah also asks about a mother-in-law who left while expecting.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעְלָהּ וְצָרָתָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: A woman whose husband and co-wife went overseas,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman whose husband and rival wife traveled to a country overseas, and witnesses

chunks.en: and people came and told her, "Your husband died":
chunks.st: came and told her: Your husband died,

chunks.en: she may not marry and may not do yibum
chunks.st: she shall not marry any other man, in case she requires levirate marriage with her brother-in-law, i.e., yavam, in which case she is prohibited from marrying anyone else.

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁתֵּדַע שֶׁמָּא מְעֻבֶּרֶת הִיא צָרָתָהּ.
chunks.en: until she knows if her co-wife is expecting a baby.
chunks.explain: If the co-wife has a baby, there is no yibum.
chunks.st: And she also shall not enter into levirate marriage until she knows whether she, i.e., her rival wife, is pregnant.
chunks.stMore: If her rival wife bears a child to her late husband, she does not have a levirate bond with her brother-in-law, and she is therefore prohibited from marrying him.

chunks.en: If she had a mother-in-law overseas,
chunks.st: If she had a mother-in-law overseas, but her late husband had no brothers,

chunks.en: she does not need to worry.
chunks.explain: That a new brother-in-law was born.
chunks.st: she need not be concerned that a brother to her husband may have been born. But if her mother-in-law

chunks.en: If she left expecting a baby, she must worry.
chunks.st: departed from her town pregnant, this widow should be concerned that perhaps her late husband now has a brother, with whom she is obligated in levirate marriage.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says: Even in such a case

chunks.en: she does not need to worry.
chunks.st: she need not be concerned and may marry whomever she wishes.

summary: Two sisters-in-law each say her own husband died. Each is believed about her own husband, but not about the other's husband, who is her yavam. The mishnah explains when they may remarry.

chunks.en: Two sisters-in-law:
chunks.st: If there are two sisters-in-law married to two childless brothers who testify about their marital status, and

chunks.en: this one says, "My husband died,"
chunks.st: this one says: My husband died,

chunks.en: and that one says, "My husband died."
chunks.st: and that one says: My husband died, although each one of them is deemed credible with regard to her own status as a widow,

chunks.he: זוֹ אֲסוּרָה מִפְּנֵי בַעְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ
chunks.en: This one is forbidden because of that one's husband,
chunks.st: this one is prohibited from marrying due to the possibility that the husband of that other sister may be alive, obligating her in levirate marriage,

chunks.he: וְזוֹ אֲסוּרָה מִפְּנֵי בַעְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ.
chunks.en: and that one is forbidden because of this one's husband.
chunks.explain: A sister-in-law is not believed about the other one.
chunks.st: and that one is prohibited from marrying due to the husband of this sister, according to the same rationale.
chunks.stMore: Although each is accorded credibility as to her own husband’s death, the halakha is that sisters-in-law are among the five types of women not accorded credibility with regard to each other’s permissibility to marry because of possible conflicts of interest. If

chunks.en: If this one has witnesses and that one does not,
chunks.st: this one has witnesses to her husband’s death, and that one does not have witnesses,

chunks.en: the one who has witnesses
chunks.st: then the one who has witnesses

chunks.en: is forbidden, and the one who has no witnesses
chunks.st: is prohibited from marrying, as there are no witnesses to the death of her yavam to exempt her from levirate marriage;

chunks.he: מֻתֶּרֶת. לָזוֹ בָנִים וְלָזוֹ אֵין בָּנִים,
chunks.en: is allowed. If this one has children and that one does not,
chunks.st: but the one who has no witnesses is permitted to marry based on her own testimony that her husband died combined with the witnesses’ testimony exempting her from levirate marriage. If this one has children and that one has no children,

chunks.en: the one who has children
chunks.st: then the one with children

chunks.en: is allowed, and the one who has no children
chunks.st: is permitted to marry, as she herself is deemed credible with regard to her husband’s death, and her children exempt her from levirate marriage.

chunks.en: is forbidden. If they did yibum and the yevamin died,
chunks.st: But the one without children is prohibited from marrying, as the death of her yavam has not been corroborated independently of her sister-in-law’s testimony. If there were two additional yevamin with whom these two widows entered into levirate marriage, and then the yevamin died childless,

chunks.en: they may not marry.
chunks.st: the women are prohibited from marrying, since the concern about an additional living yavam still remains.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: "Since they were allowed to the yevamin,
chunks.st: Since these women were permitted to marry the living brothers-in-law, as the testimony of each was deemed credible with regard to her own status,

chunks.en: they are allowed to everyone."
chunks.st: they are permitted, from then on, to marry any man because their statements, taken together, indicate that neither one is obligated to enter into levirate marriage.

summary: To say that a man died, a witness must have seen his face with his nose, saw that he really died, and saw him within three days. Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava says it depends on the case.

chunks.en: We may testify only about
chunks.st: One may testify that a man died only if he can testify about seeing

chunks.en: the face together with the nose,
chunks.st: the countenance [partzuf ] of the face with the nose, as this allows one to identify the individual with certainty.

chunks.en: even though there are
chunks.st: Although there are

chunks.en: signs on his body and his things.
chunks.st: distinguishing marks [simanim] on his body and his personal belongings, which appear to indicate his identity, one may not rely on these as identification.

chunks.he: אֵין מְעִידִין אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ,
chunks.en: We may testify only once he has died,
chunks.st: Furthermore, one may not testify that a person died until his soul actually departs.

chunks.en: even if they saw him badly wounded,
chunks.st: And even if one saw him cut open and severely wounded,

chunks.en: or hung, or a wild animal eating him.
chunks.explain: He might still live, so we cannot say he died.
chunks.st: or crucified, or with a wild animal eating parts of him, he may not testify that he died.

chunks.he: אֵין מְעִידִין אֶלָּא עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים.
chunks.en: We may testify only up to three days.
chunks.explain: After that, the face may change and be hard to know.
chunks.st: Additionally, one may testify to someone’s death only when the body was witnessed up to three days following death and not after that, since the appearance may change due to decomposition.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava says: One cannot establish general guidelines for this matter because

chunks.en: "Not every person, and not every
chunks.st: not every person,

chunks.en: place, and not every time, is the same."
chunks.st: nor every place, nor every hour is identical. Decomposition is not uniform. It occurs at different rates in different situations.

summary: If a man fell into water and was not seen again, we cannot be sure he died. The mishnah tells stories of people who fell into water, and when their wives were allowed to remarry.

chunks.en: If he fell into water,
chunks.st: If a man fell into the water and did not come out,

chunks.en: whether it has an end
chunks.st: whether the body of water has a visible end

chunks.en: or it has no end,
chunks.st: or does not have a visible end,

chunks.en: his wife is forbidden.
chunks.explain: She may not remarry, because he might have come out somewhere.
chunks.st: his wife is prohibited from remarrying. There is no absolute proof that the man died, as it is possible that he emerged from the water some distance away.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:

chunks.en: "It once happened that someone fell into the big pit,
chunks.st: An incident occurred involving a certain person who fell into the Great Cistern

chunks.en: and came up after three days."
chunks.st: and emerged only after three days. This is evidence that sometimes one may survive a fall into water, even when everyone assumes he is dead.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: "It once happened that a blind man went down to tovel in a cave,
chunks.st: An incident occurred involving a blind man who descended to immerse for ritual purity in a cave,

chunks.en: and the one leading him went down after him,
chunks.st: and his guide descended after him, and they disappeared there,

chunks.en: and they stayed long enough to have died,
chunks.st: and they remained there long enough for their souls to have departed, and the Sages

chunks.en: and they let their wives remarry."
chunks.st: permitted their wives to marry because they had disappeared into the water and not emerged.

chunks.he: וְשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְעַסְיָא בְּאֶחָד שֶׁשִּׁלְשְׁלוּהוּ לַיָּם,
chunks.en: Another time in Asya, they let a man down into the sea,
chunks.st: And there was another incident in Asya in which they lowered a certain man into the sea on a rope,

chunks.en: and only his leg came up in their hands.
chunks.st: and when they pulled the rope back to land only his leg came up in their hands, and they were not certain whether he was alive or dead.

chunks.en: The Sages said,
chunks.st: The Sages said: If his leg was cut

chunks.en: if it was from the knee and up,
chunks.st: from the knee and above, his wife

chunks.en: she may marry. If it was from the knee and down,
chunks.st: may marry, as he did not survive such a wound; if his leg was cut only

chunks.en: she may not marry.
chunks.st: from the knee and below, she may not marry.

summary: We may rely on hearing people talk about a man's death, even if they did not mean to testify. Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava says a non-Jew is believed only if he was just talking, not testifying.

chunks.en: Even if he heard women saying,
chunks.st: Even if one heard from the women, who were saying:

chunks.en: "So-and-so died,"
chunks.st: So-and-so died,

chunks.en: that is enough. Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: this is sufficient in order to testify to his death. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even if he heard children saying,
chunks.st: Even if one heard from the children, who were saying:

chunks.en: "We are going to give a hesped
chunks.st: We are going to eulogize

words.note: A speech about someone who died.

chunks.en: and bury so-and-so."
chunks.st: and bury so-and-so, that is also sufficient. Furthermore, one may rely upon someone mentioning that a man died, regardless of

chunks.he: בֵּין שֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּוֵּן וּבֵין שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְכַּוֵּן.
chunks.en: Whether he means to testify or not.
chunks.st: whether the speaker intends to testify and thereby allow the man’s wife to remarry or whether he does not intend to offer formal testimony.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava says:

chunks.en: a Jew is believed even if he means to testify,
chunks.st: With regard to a Jew who offers this information, it may be relied upon even if he intends for his statement to be considered formal testimony.

chunks.en: but a non-Jew, if he meant to testify,
chunks.st: However, with regard to a gentile, if he intended to testify,

chunks.en: his testimony does not count.
chunks.st: his testimony is not considered valid testimony. His statement is relied upon only when he does not intend to state it as formal testimony.

summary: We may testify by candlelight or moonlight, and even rely on a voice whose speaker is not seen. The mishnah tells two stories where a wife was allowed to remarry this way.

chunks.en: We may testify by candlelight or moonlight,
chunks.st: Witnesses may testify that an individual died even if they saw his corpse only by candlelight or by moonlight.

chunks.en: and we let a woman marry because of a voice from nowhere.
chunks.st: And the court may allow a woman to marry based on the statement of a disembodied voice proclaiming that her husband died.

words.note: A voice heard without seeing who spoke.

chunks.en: It once happened that someone stood on
chunks.st: There was an incident with regard to a certain individual

chunks.en: the top of a mountain and said,
chunks.st: who stood at the top of a mountain and said:

chunks.en: "So-and-so, son of so-and-so,
chunks.st: So-and-so, son of so-and-so,

chunks.en: from such a place, died."
chunks.st: from such and such a place died.

chunks.en: They went and found no one there,
chunks.st: They went and found no person there, but even so

chunks.en: and they let his wife remarry.
chunks.st: they relied upon the statement and allowed the wife of the individual declared dead to marry.

chunks.en: Another time in Tzalmon, a man said,
chunks.st: And there was another incident in Tzalmon, a city in the Galilee, where a particular man said:

chunks.he: אֲנִי אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי בֶּן אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי,
chunks.en: "I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so;
chunks.st: I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so.

chunks.en: a snake bit me,
chunks.st: A snake bit me

chunks.en: and I am dying."
chunks.st: and I am dying.

chunks.en: They went and could not recognize him,
chunks.st: And they went and found his corpse but could not recognize him,

chunks.en: and they let his wife remarry.
chunks.st: yet they went ahead and allowed his wife to marry based on what he said in his dying moments.

summary: Rabbi Akiva tells how the Sages came to allow a woman to remarry on the word of one witness. Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva argue, and the mishnah tells a story about an innkeeper.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: "When I went down to Neharde'a to add a month to the year,
chunks.st: When I descended to Neharde’a, in Babylonia, to intercalate the year,

chunks.en: I found Nechemyah of Beis Deli.
chunks.st: I found the Sage Neḥemya of Beit D’li.

chunks.en: He said to me,
chunks.st: He said to me:

chunks.he: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁאֵין מַשִּׂיאִין אֶת הָאִשָּׁה בְאֶרֶץ
chunks.en: 'I heard that in Eretz
chunks.st: I heard that the Sages

chunks.en: Yisrael they do not let a woman remarry on the word of one witness,
chunks.st: in Eretz Yisrael do not allow a woman to remarry based on the testimony of a single witness,

chunks.en: except for Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava.'
chunks.st: except for Yehuda ben Bava.

chunks.en: And I told him,
chunks.st: And I told him:

chunks.en: 'That is so.'
chunks.st: That is so.

chunks.en: He said to me,
chunks.st: He said to me:

chunks.en: 'Tell them in my name:
chunks.st: Tell the Sages in my name:

chunks.en: you know that the land is full of armies.
chunks.explain: So he could not come himself.
chunks.st: You know that the country is confounded by army troops, and I cannot come myself. I declare that

chunks.en: I have a kabbalah from Rabban Gamliel the Elder
chunks.st: I received this tradition from Rabban Gamliel the Elder,

chunks.en: that we let a woman remarry on
chunks.st: that the court may allow a woman to remarry

chunks.en: the word of one witness.'
chunks.st: based on the testimony of a single witness. Rabbi Akiva continues:

chunks.he: וּכְשֶׁבָּאתִי וְהִרְצֵיתִי הַדְּבָרִים לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
chunks.en: And when I came and told the matter to Rabban Gamliel,
chunks.st: And when I came and presented the matter before Rabban Gamliel of Yavne, the grandson of Rabban Gamliel the Elder,

chunks.en: he was happy with my words,
chunks.st: he rejoiced at my words

chunks.he: וְאָמַר, מָצָאנוּ חָבֵר לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בָּבָא.
chunks.en: and said, 'We found a friend for Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava.'"
chunks.st: and said: We have found a companion who agrees with Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, and since his lenient opinion is no longer the opinion of a lone Sage, it may now be relied upon.

chunks.en: From this talk, Rabban Gamliel remembered
chunks.st: As a result of this event, Rabban Gamliel remembered

chunks.en: that people were killed in Tel Arza,
chunks.st: that people were murdered in Tel Arza, and

chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel then allowed their wives to remarry based on

chunks.en: And it became the way to let them remarry on
chunks.st: And from then onward

chunks.en: the word of one witness,
chunks.st: they established as protocol

chunks.en: and the way to let them remarry on a witness who heard from a witness,

chunks.st: or a maidservant’s testimony.

chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua say: The court

chunks.st: may not allow a woman to remarry

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says: The court may

chunks.st: not allow a woman to marry based on the testimony of a woman,

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to Rabbi Akiva: Do we not rely upon a woman’s testimony? After all,

chunks.en: "It once happened that some Levi'im went
chunks.st: an incident occurred involving Levites who traveled

chunks.en: to Tzoar, the city of date palms,
chunks.st: to Tzoar, the city of date palms.

chunks.en: and one of them became sick on the way,
chunks.st: And one of them became ill,

chunks.en: and they brought him to an inn.
chunks.st: and they brought him to an inn [pundak] to rest, while they continued on their travels.

chunks.en: When they came back, they said to the innkeeper, 'Where is our friend?'
chunks.st: Upon their return to the inn they said to the innkeeper, who was a woman: Where is our friend?

chunks.en: She said to them, 'He died and I buried him,'
chunks.st: She told them: He died, and I buried him.

chunks.en: and they let his wife remarry."
chunks.st: And based on her testimony they allowed his wife to remarry.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: And shouldn’t a priestess, or any Jewish woman who testifies that a man died,

chunks.en: "Should a Kohen's daughter not be like the innkeeper?"
chunks.st: be deemed as credible as an innkeeper?

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to them:

chunks.en: "When she is like the innkeeper, she will be believed.
chunks.st: When a woman will be as convincing as the innkeeper, then she shall also be deemed credible.

chunks.en: The innkeeper brought out to them his stick and his bag
chunks.st: The innkeeper brought them his staff, and his bag,

chunks.en: and the Sefer Torah he had with him."
chunks.explain: These things showed that she was telling the truth.
chunks.st: and the Torah scroll that was in his possession, thereby providing supporting evidence to reinforce her claim.
